name: PA-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: Scanlon has a large fundraising edge ($990K vs $9K)
Prediction markets price her near-certain to win
No polls or expert ratings, so uncertainty stays elevated
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Scanlon: a D+15 district, incumbency, and a massive money advantage over a barely funded challenger, with markets pricing her at 98%. With no polling to refine the estimate, the margin stays near the baseline but uncertainty remains moderately wide.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Scanlon or an unusually strong national Republican environment could narrow the margin, though not plausibly enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Incumbent Mary Gay Scanlon (D) is running.

overview:
Mary Gay Scanlon seeks another term in a Delaware County-area district that leans Democratic by about 15 points, and she enters the general election with every structural advantage. She has raised nearly $1 million and holds about $449,000 in cash, while Republican Nicholas Manganaro has raised under $10,000 with no outside spending on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast rests on district partisanship, incumbency, and money. Prediction markets give Scanlon roughly a 98% chance of winning. The expected margin is about 23 points, with enough uncertainty to acknowledge the absence of polling but no realistic path to an upset.
